answer: An orchard earns fruit by carrying water; so must a ballot. Each ballot becomes a relay on the ocean of traffic: five rotating samplers, Tor-style, watch it serve real traffic for 20 minutes a tide, 5 times, and take the median — a ballot under 2 Mbps loses its $25 bond. A farm squeezing 10,000 ballots through one 1 Gbps pipe dies by the bandwidth check: each measures 100 kbps against the 2 Mbps floor, so 10,000 bonds — $250,000 — burn in one tide. An ember no one tends goes cold: a ballot's proof must be rekindled every tide by fresh measurements, never reused. One pipe, one orchard row.
